title: The family pantry
description: Seeing what is in stock at home and when it was last updated, and checking the amounts before the next trip.

blocks.text: Before a trip the family opens the shared stock and sees what was checked recently. For one item a “have it” mark is enough, for another a quantity or the date it was opened. There is no need to demand the same precision from every product.

quote.text: I always forget what I have and often buy duplicates because I forget what’s in my fridge. This app has single handedly changed the game for me. I now know what I have, am reminded when things are about to expire, and know what I need to make next.

blocks.text: Remembering what is left at home

Filling it in the first time can be sped up by scanning, but the entries have to be easy to correct from any device in the household. When the shopping is being put together, the app offers to check an amount that has not been updated in a long time rather than subtracting it automatically.
Not turning the kitchen into a warehouse

The main question to test is whether people will keep the stock up to date after the first inventory. If maintaining the catalog takes longer than looking in the fridge, it is worth keeping only the products that are often forgotten or bought twice.
